title: The Half-Way Balance
mathematical_role: Make element frequencies, the one-half threshold, and the incidence double-count identity literal on one exact family.
learning_objective: Connect row incidences and column frequencies to the identity sum_x freq_F(x)=sum_A |A|, while seeing why an average identity alone does not prove the universal conjecture.
literal_semantics: The same six-set family F has frequencies 4, 3, and 2 for a, b, and c.
The displayed equality Σ_x freq_F(x)=Σ_A |A| holds exactly for the example.
nonliteral_semantics: Bar geometry encodes only the labeled occurrence counts and not theorem strength.

notes: Exact finite-example data are reproduced by tests/test_visual_pedagogy_batch1_candidates.py.
Imported theorem-terrain language remains bounded by the documentary source and does not admit a new external claim.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG generator v1
reproducibility_notes: The generator uses no network, randomness, timestamps, fonts embedded as files, or external data.
Repository tests compare generator output byte-for-byte with the committed SVG candidate.

accessibility.alt_text: Frequency bars and a six-row incidence matrix show counts four, three, and two against a half threshold of three; column and row-size sums both equal nine.
accessibility.long_description: The left side shows frequency bars for a, b, and c with exact counts 4/6, 3/6, and 2/6 and a dashed threshold at 3. The right side shows the six sets as rows of an incidence matrix. The column count total and the sum of row sizes both equal 9, displaying the standard incidence double-count identity.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: For the displayed family, the incidence matrix, frequencies, threshold, and double-count totals are exact.
not_claimed: That the double-count identity alone proves Frankl's conjecture

supersession_reason: Ground the half-way metaphor in an exact incidence matrix, frequency bars, and the incidence double-count identity.
